C01.help: Chooses which overworld the player explores: the first quest's, the second quest's, a mix of the two, or one picked for each seed.

C02.help: Chooses where the dungeon layouts come from: the first quest, the second quest, a mix, newly generated shapes, a mix with shapes, or one picked for each seed.

C03.help: Chooses what the people in caves and dungeons say: the original lines, helpful hints, community lines, misleading hints, a mix, nothing at all, or one picked for each seed.

C04.help: Chooses the screen the player starts on: the usual one, a shuffled one (easy or full shuffle), or the wooden-sword cave's screen.

C05.help: Chooses which entrances lead somewhere new: none, only the dungeon doors, only the other caves, all of them, or one picked for each seed.

C06.help: Chooses how widely items are shuffled: not at all, among dungeon items only, within each dungeon, or across dungeons, caves and the overworld together.

C07.help: Chooses how the wooden sword works: as usual, as the only sword, never given, no swords at all, or one picked for each seed.

C08.help: Chooses what opens level 9: 1 to 8 Triforce pieces, nothing (it is open), a random count in a range, specific pieces, an item instead of pieces, or one picked for each seed.

C09.help: Chooses how enemies' hit points change: not at all, by up to 2 or up to 4 for each kind of enemy, all to zero, or one picked for each seed.

C10.help: Chooses how bosses' hit points change: not at all, by up to 2 or up to 4 for each boss, all to zero, or one picked for each seed.

C11.help: Chooses an item that is always found at the secret Armos spot, or none.

C12.help: Chooses an item that is always found in the coast cave, or none; the Ladder is not allowed there.

C13.help: Chooses an item that is always found in the white-sword cave, or none.

C14.help: Chooses how dungeon rooms are shuffled: not at all, within each dungeon, between dungeons, or one picked for each seed.

C15.help: Chooses how items and characters look: as usual, a fun percentage, shuffled sprites, or one picked for each seed.

C16.help: Chooses how many hearts the player starts with: 1 to 16, or a random number from 1 to 5.

C17.help: Limits how many of the chosen starting items the player really gets: all of them, at most 0 to 20, or a random limit from 0 to 20.

C18.help: Chooses how many Triforce pieces the player starts with: 0 to 8, or a random number.

C19.help: Chooses what a red bubble does to the player: takes the sword away as in the original game, reverses the controls, slows the player down, or one picked for each seed.

C20.help: Sets the fewest hearts the white-sword cave can ask for (4 to 6).

C21.help: Sets the most hearts the white-sword cave can ask for (4 to 6).

C22.help: Sets the fewest hearts the magical-sword cave can ask for (10 to 14).

C23.help: Sets the most hearts the magical-sword cave can ask for (10 to 14).

C24.help: Sets the fewest Triforce pieces level 9 can ask for when it asks for a random count or for specific pieces.

C25.help: Sets the most Triforce pieces level 9 can ask for when it asks for a random count or for specific pieces.

C26.help: Chooses an item that is always found inside level 9 (the first of two), or none.

C27.help: Chooses an item that is always found inside level 9 (the second of two), or none.

B01.help: With it on, the recorder takes the player to the dungeons' new entrances; with it off, it works as usual.

B02.help: With it on, the wooden-sword cave can be at any hidden cave spot; with it off, it is not moved to one.

B03.help: With it on, the wooden-sword cave can be hidden behind blocks; with it off, it never is.

B04.help: With it on, the take-any-road caves trade places; with it off, they stay where they are.

B05.help: With it on, the tiles that hide secret entrances move; with it off, they stay where they are.

B06.help: With it on, the overworld is mirrored; with it off, it is laid out as usual.

B07.help: With it on, the recorder takes the player to dungeons not yet beaten; with it off, it works as usual.

B08.help: With it on, shop wares move between shops and their prices vary; with it off, each shop sells its usual wares.

B09.help: With it on, shops can also sell extra candles; with it off, they don't.

B10.help: With it on, the number of hearts the white-sword and magical-sword caves ask for changes with each seed; with it off, they ask for the usual number.

B11.help: With it on, the money-making game's amounts change with each seed; with it off, they are the usual ones.

B12.help: With it on, the bomb-upgrade person's price and number of extra bombs change with each seed; with it off, they are the usual ones.

B13.help: With it on, the item under the secret Armos is shuffled with the others; with it off, it is the usual item.

B14.help: Changes nothing in the game: it is shown and kept in the flag string only.

B15.help: With it on, the items in dungeon rooms are shuffled within each level; with it off, they stay in their rooms.

B16.help: Changes nothing in the game: it is shown and kept in the flag string only (heart containers are shuffled by the item shuffle setting instead).

B17.help: With it on, bombs, rupees and keys are shuffled along with the other items; with it off, they are not.

B18.help: With it on, the player has to beat Ganon to finish; with it off, the game ends as usual.

B19.help: With it on, the hints given by people in dungeons are swapped around between them; with it off, each person keeps their hint.

B20.help: With it on, generated dungeons can also use second-quest rooms; with it off, they use only first-quest rooms.

B21.help: With it on, generated dungeons also use the second quest's mix of doors; with it off, they don't.

B22.help: With it on, some people in dungeon rooms become merchants who ask for life or money; with it off, they are as usual.

B23.help: With it on, what those merchants ask for changes with each seed; with it off, it is the usual amount.

B24.help: With it on, the dungeon numbers are hidden; with it off, they are shown.

B25.help: With it on, important items can be inside level 9; with it off, they can't.

B26.help: With it on, a dungeon can start in a different room; with it off, each dungeon starts in its usual room.

B27.help: With it on, the dungeons get different colours; with it off, they keep their usual colours.

B28.help: With it on, the hungry goriya that wants food can be in a different dungeon room; with it off, it stays in its usual room.

B29.help: With it on, the people who sell bomb upgrades in dungeons are moved around; with it off, they stay where they are.

B30.help: With it on, most open staircases are removed; with it off, they stay.

B31.help: With it on, the monsters on the overworld screens are shuffled; with it off, each screen has its usual monsters.

B32.help: With it on, each dungeon's monsters are shuffled between its rooms; with it off, they stay in their rooms.

B33.help: With it on, Ganon and Zelda are moved by those shuffles too; with it off, they stay where they are.

B34.help: With it on, the bosses are shuffled; with it off, each boss is in its usual place.

B35.help: With it on, level 9's monsters also move between levels; with it off, they stay in level 9.

B36.help: With it on, monsters can move from one dungeon to another; with it off, each dungeon keeps its own monsters.

B37.help: With it on, second-quest monsters can appear in generated dungeons; with it off, they don't.

B38.help: With it on, the groups that decide what enemies drop are shuffled; with it off, they are as usual.

B39.help: With it on, enemies can drop important items; with it off, they don't.

B40.help: With it on, the groups of bosses are mixed up; with it off, they are as usual.

B41.help: With it on, Ganon has no hit points; with it off, Ganon's hit points are as usual.

B42.help: With it on, the groups of enemies are shuffled; with it off, they are as usual.

B43.help: With it on, the overworld screens' monsters are redrawn from the overworld group; with it off, they are as usual.

B44.help: With it on, how often items drop is random; with it off, it is the usual rate.

B45.help: With it on, every enemy has the most health possible; with it off, enemy health is as usual.

B46.help: With it on, every boss has the most health possible; with it off, boss health is as usual.

B47.help: With it on, the Book of Magic turns the wand's fire into an explosion; with it off, it makes fire as usual.

B48.help: With it on, carrying the Book of Magic lets the player understand old men; with it off, it doesn't.

B49.help: With it on, holding the Book of Magic counts as having every dungeon's map; with it off, each map has to be found.

B50.help: With it on, the game plays in blackout mode; with it off, it doesn't.

B51.help: With it on, the game prints quest information; with it off, it doesn't.

B52.help: With it on, the sword always shoots a beam; with it off, the beam works as usual.

B53.help: With it on, any hit knocks the player out; with it off, damage is as usual.

B54.help: With it on, people's text appears faster; with it off, it appears at the usual speed.

B55.help: With it on, the player's health is hidden; with it off, it is shown.

B56.help: With it on, items that enemies drop can be destroyed; with it off, they can't.

B57.help: With it on, the player starts with the Raft (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B58.help: With it on, the player starts with the Bow (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B59.help: With it on, the player starts with 8 bombs; with it off, bombs have to be found.

B60.help: With it on, the player starts with the Recorder (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B61.help: With it on, the player starts with the Bait (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B62.help: With it on, the player starts with the Magical Key (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B63.help: With it on, the player starts with the Letter (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B64.help: With it on, the player starts with the Power Bracelet (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B65.help: With it on, the player starts with the Ladder (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B66.help: With it on, the player starts with the Wand (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B67.help: With it on, the player starts with the Book of Magic (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B68.help: With it on, the player starts with the wooden sword (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B69.help: With it on, the player starts with the white sword (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B70.help: With it on, the player starts with the magical sword (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B71.help: With it on, the player starts with the wooden arrow (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B72.help: With it on, the player starts with the Silver Arrow (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B73.help: With it on, the player starts with the blue candle (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B74.help: With it on, the player starts with the red candle (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B75.help: With it on, the player starts with the blue ring (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B76.help: With it on, the player starts with the red ring (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B77.help: With it on, the player starts with the wooden Boomerang (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B78.help: With it on, the player starts with the Magical Boomerang (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B79.help: With it on, extra bosses are added; with it off, there are the usual bosses.

B80.help: With it on, the rupees the player carries change their speed; with it off, they don't.

B81.help: With it on, the game forces an overworld block for an item; with it off, it doesn't.

B82.help: Encodes most dungeon and overworld data so ROM editors and map viewers (like the Z1R Visualizer) can't read it. Gameplay is exactly the same. This isn't cheat-proof: a determined person can still decode the data.

B83.help: With it on, numbers are hidden; with it off, they are shown.

B84.help: With it on, the game prevents slipping through walls while the screen scrolls; with it off, it doesn't.

B85.help: With it on, the player starts with the magical shield (within the limit on starting items); with it off, it has to be found.

B86.help: With it on, generated dungeon shapes are not sorted by size; with it off, they are.

B87.help: With it on, bridges are added over the river; with it off, the river is as usual.

B88.help: With it on, there is a shortcut through the Lost Woods; with it off, there isn't.

B89.help: With it on, the hidden tiles on the overworld change; with it off, they are as usual.

B90.help: With it on, the bomb upgrade adds more bombs; with it off, it adds the usual number.

B91.help: With it on, generated dungeons can use universal drops; with it off, they don't.
